page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top, with the page number at the top left. Below it a full-width text block: four paragraphs, a rule, a large numbered heading, and then the opening paragraph of the next section, which carries a large initial V. No marginal notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: Ne dedas nos Impot entiæ affectuum, & no-bis, & aliis exitiosæ.
Purga nostros Intellectus, ut veritatem tuam videant, tum Rationis ut homines, tum Religionis ut Christiani: & sic omnium corda inclines, ut servemus unitatem Spiritus in vinculo pacis.
Tolle illam in te Inimicitiam, cordibus nostris nimis infitam, & illam indas charitatem, quam exercere mutuo debemus.
Remove quæ ita valde commeriti sumus Belli mala, & illam Pacem Largiaris, quam Ille noster Pacificus Christus unice potest mereri.
main_text.head: 19. De vario Belli successu ,· Victoriis & Cladibus.
main_text.p: VArii huius Belli Infœlicissimi Eventus occasionem suggesserunt varia meditandi. Placuit Deo nō-nunquam experiri me victoriis, fusis ho-stibus & profligatis, eo fine, ut discerem simul gratè agnoscere & moderatè uti ea Ipsius Potentia, qui est vere Dominus exer-citum, potens (ubi collibuisset) repri-mere

page.notes: The leading mark "*" before "Remove" is probably a stray printer's mark or fleck, not a note reference, so it is left out. The large V of "Varii" is a decorative initial; it is written as V. The page number "170" is printed in an ornate form and is uncertain. A small centred dot below the last line is a printer's mark, not text. The right edge shows the book's binding and show-through, which are not transcribed. "successu" is in italic in the heading; "successu" was read as "successu" with plain s. Possible printing irregularity: "Impot entiæ" is printed with a space; kept as printed.
